quick_read.weather_md: **Weather:** 27°C high / 18°C low. Sun with the occasional late-afternoon shower. I would not lug a full-size umbrella; a compact folder in the bag handles any surprise.
quick_read.uv_md: **UV:** 7 today, climbs to 8 mid-week. **SPF 30+ broad spectrum** before you leave the hotel. Reapply after lunch if you've been outside — your forehead and ears burn first, sir. A cap is not optional in Central Park.
quick_read.uv_advisory_md: *📎 Goose Investigation Bureau — sourcing UV from EPA + Cancer Research UK. UV 1–2 = no protection needed. UV 3+ = sunscreen + shade + hat + sunglasses. UV 8+ = limit midday sun. UV 11+ = stay out of midday sun entirely.*
quick_read.budget_hint_md: **Daily budget — $250 average.** With my picks below, that's real. Save: subway instead of cabs ($30/day), deli breakfast instead of sit-down ($20/day). Splurge: a tasting menu pushes you toward $400 quickly. **Caveat: the World Cup is in town. Hotels are running elevated — book yesterday.**
quick_read.intro_md: > *Sir, I've reviewed your calendar, cross-referenced advisories, and pulled the establishments worth your time. The World Cup overlay reshaped the city this month — I've factored it in throughout. Below is the full dossier.*
quick_read.do_now_md:
**Do now:**
- **Jun 16 + Jun 22 = World Cup match nights at MetLife.** France vs Senegal Jun 16 3pm; Norway vs Senegal Jun 22 8pm. If you're not at the stadium, book restaurant reservations *before* 7pm those nights — watch parties pack every bar in Midtown and Hell's Kitchen.
- **Activate contactless before you land.** OMNY tap with your phone for the subway, $2.90 flat. Apple Pay and Google Pay both clear the turnstile.
- **Cash is a courtesy, not a king.** Pull **$60** day one. Almost everything takes tap. The cash is for doormen, bartenders, the bodega guy.
quick_read.restaurant_hook_md: **The Places to Eat list below is the move.** These are Michelin Guide picks — most are not starred, which is the point. Excellent food, accessible bookings, not $400-per-person territory. Book on Resy or Tock as soon as you finish reading.

happening.news_md:
- **🏆 FIFA World Cup 2026 active — Jun 11 to Jul 19, citywide overlay.** MetLife Stadium across the river hosts eight matches. Hotel rates elevated, NYPD presence heavier in Times Square and Midtown, expanded summer ferry service active, and Parks Department restricting new event permits through Jul 19 to free up security resources. None of this is trip-canceling — it's the texture of the month. [src 1, 2]
- **New administration — Mayor Zohran Mamdani.** Sworn in Jan 1 2026, first summer in office. Public-safety priorities shifting. No major announced protests in your window. Check `nyc.gov/mayors-office/news` before you leave for anything fresh. [src 3]
- **MTA G line service changes — ongoing 2026.** If you're staying or eating in Brooklyn/Queens, check `mta.info/alerts` for shuttle replacements on the days you plan to ride it. [src 4]
happening.sports_md:
- **⚽ World Cup at MetLife — Jun 16, 3pm ET: France vs Senegal.** Day 2 of your trip. Train from Penn Station to Secaucus Junction, then free stadium shuttle. Tickets resale-only at this point; entry-level around $400+. Watch parties at most Midtown sports bars if you skip the stadium. [src 2]
- **⚽ World Cup at MetLife — Jun 22, 8pm ET: Norway vs Senegal.** Final day. If you're flying out earlier, skip; otherwise an evening option. [src 2]
- **⚾ Mets vs Cubs — Jun 22, 7:10pm at Citi Field.** $25–50 nosebleeds, 7 train to Mets-Willets Point. Mets are middling, but the stadium experience holds up. [src 5]
- **🏀 NBA Draft — Jun 23–24 at Barclays Center.** Just past your dates, but if you extend, Brooklyn runs loud those nights. [src 6]
happening.entertainment_md:
- **Pride Month, all five boroughs.** Pride March on Sunday Jun 28. Citywide events from your arrival day onward: free concerts, parties, panels. West Village + Chelsea wall-to-wall Fri–Sun. [src 7]
- **Photoville on the Brooklyn Bridge waterfront.** Free outdoor photography festival inside shipping containers, family-friendly, active in your window. [src 7]
- **NewFest Pride film festival — five days, late June.** LGBTQ+ premieres, Q&As, outdoor screenings. Check NewFest's calendar the week of. [src 7]
- **Madison Square Garden in your window.** Lineup shifts weekly; check `msg.com/calendar` for the nights you're free. [src 8]

brief.watch_md:
- **Top of the Rock at sunset — ~$45.** Better than the Empire State view, because you can see the Empire State *in* your photo. Book the slot 30 minutes before sunset. South-facing deck.
- **High Line + Little Island combo — FREE.** Walk Chelsea Market to Hudson Yards, loop back via Little Island. Photo: Little Island west pier at sunset.
- **The Whispering Gallery at Grand Central — FREE.** Niche pick, but indispensable. Stand at one corner of the tiled archway outside the Oyster Bar; have your companion stand diagonally opposite. Whisper into the wall. The voice arrives clean, as if they're beside you. Gustavino tile, perfect acoustic geometry. Five minutes, never stops being strange.
- **Brooklyn Bridge — walk Brooklyn to Manhattan — FREE.** Skyline grows as you cross. Reverse of what tourists do. Photo: Pebble Beach on the Brooklyn side before you start.
- **Central Park — Bethesda Terrace — FREE.** Tile ceiling, fountain, buskers. Underrated by the photo-nerd crowd.
brief.eat_md:
*Most are Guide-listed, not starred. The point is good food, not gold-card territory.*

- **Le Bernardin** — Three stars (yes, the exception). Seafood. Book 6 weeks ahead for prime time; lunch is easier. *(~$200+ pp lunch, $400+ dinner)*
- **Atomix** — Two stars. Korean tasting menu. Tock booking, drops at midnight 30 days out. Set the alarm. *(~$375 pp tasting)*
- **Cote** — One star. Korean steakhouse, loud, fun, expensive. Weekdays seat easier than weekends. *(~$130 pp)*
- **Via Carota** — Bib Gourmand. No reservations, walk-in only. Line up before 5:30 or accept defeat. *(~$55 pp)*
- **Don Angie** — Guide listed. Italian-American with style, lasagna pinwheels. Resy four weeks out. *(~$80 pp)*
brief.knowing_md:
- **Transit — subway first, app second.** The subway beats a cab below 14th Street, especially Friday through Sunday. Uber and Lyft both work normally in NYC; no local-app trickery here, unlike Rome. Yellow cabs via Curb app or street hail. Check MTA service alerts before any weekend trip — there's always track work somewhere.
- **Tipping is a tax, not a thank-you. 20% baseline.** Restaurants, bars ($2/drink), taxis, hotel housekeeping ($2–5/night), doormen with bags. Skipping reads as hostile, not frugal.
- **Bodega coffee is a religion, not a transaction.** Walk in, ask for "regular," receive coffee with milk and two sugars. Specify "black" if that's what you want. $1.50, tastes like the city. Skip the Starbucks line entirely.
- **Don't stand on the left of an escalator.** Stand right, walk left. Tourists who block the left receive a particular kind of New York stare.
- **Tap water is excellent — refuse the bottle.** NYC tap is mountain-watershed clean. Restaurants pour it free; some servers attempt to upsell sparkling. You may decline.

budget_usd.notes: Mid = boutique hotel below 50th ($180), 1 sit-down + 1 deli ($65), subway + 1 museum ($35). Cocktails at $18–22 each accelerate the count.
